What the data shows

Twelve months of customer orders, supplier purchases and month-end stock, drawn with Python.

How the model was built

  1. Added up the kilograms sold for each product in each month: 780 product-months.
  2. Gave the model its inputs: last month's demand, the product's average so far, price, season flags, category, storage and cut group.
  3. Trained a linear regression on Dec 25 to Jun 26 and tested it on Jul 26 to Sep 26, months it had never seen.
  4. Compared it with two simple rules: repeat last month, or use the product's average.
  5. Retrained on all months to forecast Oct 26 to Dec 26.
28.9%forecast error on test months
40.4%error if we repeat last month
0.67R² on test months
105 kgaverage miss per item per month

Reading the model

The model works on the log of demand, so a busy item and a quiet item are treated fairly. A product's own average is by far the strongest input, which is why steady sellers are predicted best.

On the test months it is about 12 points more accurate than repeating last month. Individual items can still miss by a few hundred kilograms, and the largest misses are in high-volume months.

Forecast

The solid blue line over the shaded test months shows how the model did on data it had not seen. The dashed line is the forecast.

Reading the forecast

Dec 26 is the highest month because the model learned a December and winter-season lift from a single year of data. Treat it as an upper estimate until a second year is available.

Prices are assumed to stay at recent levels, and no promotions or new customers are included.

Purchase plan

Target stock is next month's forecast plus 25% safety stock. Stock is the month-end figure for Sep 26. 65 of 65 items fall short of target; the 15 largest orders are listed.

Built with Python (pandas, scikit-learn, matplotlib) from six datasets: product master, customers, customer orders, suppliers, purchase orders and the monthly inventory ledger. All values are sample data generated for demonstration.

Limits: the model has only 12 months of history, so it cannot fully learn seasonal patterns. Two or more years of data would make the forecast more reliable.
